subject: KeplerISV connector failures — request for expedited support coordination
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@keplerisv.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: simon@keplerisv.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Kepler connector errors impacting customer X (prod)

Hi Lauren —

We're seeing a spike of 502/timeout errors from the Redwood connector when our customers hit long prompt generation flows. This started around 07:45 PT and affects five enterprise customers on our managed plan. Our engineering team captured a set of runtime traces and a small error dump (attached).

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether this is a serving-side regression or a config mismatch on our end?
- We need a short window for a joint triage call within the hour — can someone from your on-call take this?

We flagged this as high priority because customers are opening tickets; we may need an SLO credit conversation if this persists. I've included a short dump and a list of affected customer IDs in the attachment.

Thanks —
Anya Petrov
Head of Integrations, KeplerISV
anya@keplerisv.com

Attachments: kepler_error_dump_0822.log (text, 1.2MB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Anya Petrov <anya@keplerisv.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kepler connector errors impacting customer X (prod)

Anya — thanks for the quick heads up and for sending the dump.

Short summary of next steps from Redwood:
1) Mateo (cc'd) will review the logs immediately and confirm whether traces match any recent runtime rollouts.
2) Marissa (cc'd) will schedule a 30-minute triage call; suggested window 09:00–09:30 PT. Please confirm availability.
3) We will collect correlated request IDs and token-level latency samples; if this is a serving regression we will provide a hotfix plan within 4 hours.

Can you also share whether Kepler has disabled any of your prefix caching or if you've toggled batching in the last 24 hours? Those two knobs are the most common sources of divergence when we see higher tail latency.

I'll keep this thread updated — assigning INC-5873 in our systems and pulling an on-call engineer now.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Anya Petrov <anya@keplerisv.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kepler connector errors impacting customer X (prod)

On Sat, 22 Aug 2026 at 08:28 AM lauren_bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
> Can you also share whether Kepler has disabled any of your prefix caching or if you've toggled batching in the last 24 hours?

Thanks — I pulled the dump. Quick findings:
- Error pattern: repeated 504s and occasional 502s tied to late token generation for sequences >1024 tokens; KV cache misses observed in the tail.
- We did a small kernel tweak rolled to canary last night (latency-focused), but telemetry doesn't show a global rollout to production for the dedicated pools serving Kepler.

Immediate plan:
- I'll spin up an isolated replica using the previous kernel profile (rollback candidate) and run a replay of the request ids you attached. If the replica reproduces failures, we will trigger a rollback to the previous kernel across the affected pool. ETA: 2 hours.
- Marissa will run the bridge call and capture customer impact details for SLO conversation.

Anya — can you confirm whether Kepler is using pinned model versions or the latest catalog model? If you are on a floating model tag we may need to pin until we finish the root-cause.

Attachments referenced: kepler_integration_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook excerpt)

— Mateo
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Anya Petrov <anya@keplerisv.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: KeplerISV — triage summary and customer remediation path

Hi all — thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and owner assignments so the execs on both sides have a single source of truth: 

What happened:
- Spike in tail latency for long-generation prompts caused repeated 504s for five managed accounts. Root cause: interaction between a recent optional kernel performance tweak and certain workload patterns that surface KV cache misses at high sequence lengths.

Actions completed (Sat):
- Mateo validated failure against a rollback replica and rolled the canary kernel back on the affected pool at 11:45 PT. Error rate returned to baseline within ~12 minutes.
- Kepler confirmed they were on a floating model tag; they pinned to model v2.1.3 to stabilize behavior.

Pending actions and timeline:
- Redwood will run a focused regression test across the full sequence-length distribution and produce a short post-triage report by Tue EOD (owner: Mateo).
- Kepler to provide a customer-facing summary and any outstanding refund/credit asks by Mon EOD (owner: Anya).
- Partnership team to open a one-time SLO credit review if Kepler submits formal credit requests (owner: Lauren).

Attachments: kepler_integration_runbook_v1.pdf (excerpt), INC-5873 post-triage notes (internal)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it here and I'll update.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Phone: +1 650-555-0123
